project.name: Markinch
project.boundarySource: Resolved named-place location with a conservative strict settlement study buffer
project.researchNotes: Sequential place 15 of 15: every required category, all four named trail providers, local HES/NRHE completeness, dates, access, transport and dogs were checked before continuing. Balbirnie House Hotel and golf course are private businesses outside the public-park offer. Balgonie Castle and Glenrothes facilities do not inflate Markinch’s settlement score. Full restaurants and pubs are not used to pad the café-led Eat category. The church toilet is clearly limited to church opening rather than presented as an always-open public convenience.

touristAppeal.label: Strong Destination
touristAppeal.summary: Markinch is a strong heritage-and-walking destination: an exceptional early-12th-century church, a 72-acre designed park, a current café, a deep signed trail network, picnic sites, two free public car parks, rail access and seasonal church facilities. The score uses only verified public experiences.
touristAppeal.dogAccessSummary: Outdoor access can work for responsible dog visits; venue-specific policies are recorded individually.

visitorHighlights.name: St Drostan’s Church
visitorHighlights.reason: An active church with an exceptional early-12th-century Scoto-Norman tower, churchyard and interpretation of Markinch’s role as Fife’s medieval capital.
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: April–October 10.30am–5.30pm; keyholder information is posted outside other times. Check before a special trip.

editorialReview.scoreRationale: St Drostan’s Church is separately assessed for visit depth, distinctiveness, presentation, journey worth, access reliability and evidence quality.

visitorHighlights.name: Balbirnie Park
